t15-11-1: 11. — The **coffee** (72) of this excellent firm has earned a well-deserved name among the **maids** (69) and the cooks, because the old **grocer** (71) roasts it himself with the greatest care.
t15-12-1: 12. — Not everyone comes to the market to buy provisions. In the picturesque coming and going of the little street that leads to the hall, you see the most varied people. Beside a good-natured **slaughterhouse man** (75) pushing a **wheelbarrow** (74) in front of him, there are two soldiers on leave, very proud to show off their bright uniforms: the **hussar** (76) in his blue **dolman** and **plumed shako**, and the **corporal of Zouaves** in baggy breeches with a **fez** on his head.
t15-13-1: 13. — The **baker** (80) , standing on the doorstep of the **bakery** (78) , has just kneaded the dough for his **bread** (79) and taken out of the oven the **croissants** (81) , the **rolls** (82) and the **round loaves** (83) that are in the window.
t15-14-1: 14. — Above the bakery lives a skilful **seamstress** (84) who employs several **embroiderers** (85) . Next to her lives a **laundress and ironer** (86) , who starches the **linen** (88) after washing and drying it, and presses it with an **iron** (87) .
t15-15-1: 15. — In the **butcher’s shop** (89) on the ground floor, meat of every kind is sold — **mutton** (90) , **beef** (94) or **veal** (92) — as **legs of lamb, steaks, joints** and **chops**. The **butcher’s boy** (93) cuts up all this meat and sets aside the **marrowbones** (96) . At the door of the butcher’s stands an **oyster seller** (97) who sells **oysters** (98) . She will open them for you if you like.
t15-16-1: 16. — All these traders pay a license or a pitch fee; that is why the **policeman** (100) shows no mercy to the poor **street vegetable sellers** (99) , who compete with them by carrying about on their barrows **carrots, radishes, turnips, leeks** or **bundles of asparagus, fresh peas, spinach, sorrel, watercress** and **parsley**.
t15-17-1: 17. — The boy selling **garlic** (101) and **onions** knows very well that he too is not allowed to sell his goods near the market. He runs off, at the risk of upsetting the basket of **crabs**, **crayfish** and **shrimps** belonging to the **seller** (102) of **spiny lobsters** and **lobsters**.
t15-18-1: 18. — Everyone is bustling about and making a great din; but you can still hear clearly the call of the traveling **glazier** (103) , nor the cry of the **coalman** (104) , who has just left his cart for a moment to deliver a **sack of coal** (105) .
t16-apar-1: CHART No. 16 The Department Store. — The Bazaar. — The Toys.
t16-01-1: 1. — The new year is coming. The big shops have got ready their displays of **toys** (1) and new year presents.
t16-01-2: I asked my grandfather to take me to the bazaar to see this fine display, and he agreed.
t16-02-1: 2. — First we stopped in front of some handsome trophies of arms holding a **rifle**, a **peaked cap**, a **saber**, a **sword belt** and a pair of **epaulettes**, or else a **helmet**, a **breastplate** (3) and a **pistol** (4) . All that interested me far more than the **magic lanterns** (2) .
t16-03-1: 3. — In the same department there was a **sentry** (5) in his **sentry box**; he seemed to be standing guard over a whole cardboard menagerie. What a lot of animals there were! A **parrot** (6) on its perch, a **rhinoceros** (7) with a horn on its nose, a **reindeer** (8) , an **ostrich** (9) , a **monkey** (10) cracking a nut, a **fox** (11) carrying off a hen, a **crocodile** (12) gaping with its enormous jaws, a **camel** (13) , an elegant **greyhound** (14) , a **panther** (15) , and then two beasts I did not know, which are, I am told, a **weasel** (16) and a **hyena** (17) . There was also a **leopard** (18) and a **wolf** (21) ; close by were sweet little **rats** (19) and tiny rubber **mice** (20) . Lastly a **hippopotamus** (22) and a humped **dromedary** (23) completed the collection. I would have stayed there for hours if a splendid camp full of **tin soldiers** (29) nearby had not caught my eye.
t16-04-1: 4. — My grandfather, who is a **disabled veteran** (24) and had to leave the army after a **wound** that earned him the **military medal**, loves to tell me about the **campaigns** he took part in. He was delighted to explain to me the various movements of the little army in miniature. A group of real soldiers visiting the bazaar — an **engineer** (25) , an **alpine light infantryman** (26) in his **beret**, an infantry **sergeant major** (27) and an artillery **sergeant** (28) with a gold **stripe** on his sleeve — stopped near us to listen to the explanations.
t16-05-1: 5. — My grandfather, very proud to have such a distinguished audience, improvised a whole plan of battle.
t16-05-2: The fortified town, with its **ramparts** and **ditches**, was besieged by the **enemy army**, which, after a long **bombardment**, was preparing to **storm** it. But the **besieged**, driven to it by hunger, had attempted a **sortie** against the **camp** of the **besiegers**. Having beaten off the **attack** in a fierce **fight** around the **tents**, the **victorious** besiegers sent their **squadrons** in **pursuit** of the **defeated** attackers. The latter **retreated**, leaving the **battlefield** strewn with the **dead** and the **wounded**. **Stretcher bearers** carried the wounded off to the **field hospital** to be tended by the **surgeon**.
t16-05-3: Despite the heroic resistance of a few **battalions** that had formed **square**, the **defeat** was complete; the rest of the army **fled**, leaving many **prisoners** behind. The enemy was about to crown its **victory** by taking the town. Perhaps that would be the end of the campaign, and after an **armistice** a **peace treaty** could be signed.
t16-06-1: 6. — The young soldiers, who laughed as they listened to the veteran’s colourful tale, asked him a few more questions. As for me, I walked round the counter to look at a fine **crossbow** (32) and a **bow** (33) with its **arrow** (31) . There I found another collection of animals: two **songbirds** (34) , a clockwork **nightingale** and **warbler** singing at the top of their voices, and a series of strange beasts — a **bat** (35) , a **boa** (36) , a **tortoise** (37) , a **seal** (38) , a **whale** (39) and a **shark** (40) made of goldbeater’s skin.
t16-07-1: 7. — I did not stop long to look at them, because I had caught sight of the thing I had been dreaming of: a magnificent **puppet theater** (41) with splendid **scenery** and a delightful red **curtain**. On **stage**, two actors seemed to be playing a **part** in a most interesting **play**, because the little cardboard **spectators** in the boxes, or seated in the **stalls** and in the **pit** behind the **conductor**, were applauding warmly.
t16-07-2: Sadly, that theater was very expensive.
t16-08-1: 8. — Choosing among the toys was difficult anyway, because the windows were piled with toys of every kind: **Harlequin** (42) , **Punch** (43) , **Pierrot** (44) , **owls** (45) flapping their wings, whistling **blackbirds** (46) , barking **poodles**, a **gramophone** (47) and **puzzles**. I loved one of these toys: it showed a **sea battle** (48) in which a **ship** is attacked by **pirates** off a shore planted with **coconut palms**.
t16-09-1: 9. — I could look at all these wonders quite at my leisure, because there were only a few people in the store — barely a handful of idlers, a **dragoon** (49) , and a **collector** (50) presenting a **bill of exchange** at the main **cash desk** (51) .
t16-10-1: 10. — I asked my grandfather what the books on the shelves behind the **cashier** were for; he told me they were the **account books**.
t16-11-1: 11. — Leaving the toy department, we went to the saddlery to glance at the **saddles** (53) , **stirrups** (54) , **bridles** (55) , **bits** (56) and **riding crops**. While the **department manager** (57) gave my grandfather some information, I went to look at the display of **china** and **glassware** (58) , where there were fine **salad bowls** and delicate **teapots** (59) .
t16-12-1: 12. — To go up to the first floor, we passed behind the window of the **corsets** (60) , next to the hosiery, where very fine **drawers** (63) were laid out. Nearby, a **shop assistant** (61) was helping a **customer** (62) choose fine silk **fabrics** (64) .
t16-12-2: As I went up the stairs, I noticed that the store was decorated with Japanese **lanterns** (65) , **parasols** (66) and enormous **palms** (70) .
t16-13-1: 13. — On the first floor there was not much to see: only furniture (*) , **safes** (67) , **chests of drawers** (68) and **prams** (69) . But the general view of the store was very **entertaining**.
t16-14-1: 14. — Below us I could see the musical instruments: **harps** (71) , **guitars** (72) , **mandolins** (73) , **cornets** (74) , **clarinets** (75) , violins with their **bows** (76) and even a **bass drum** (77) . A little further on, at the stationery counter, a **student** (78) was haggling with the **shop assistant** (79) over a document case. Near them I could make out a fine **alphabet book** (80) .
t16-14-2: In the middle of the store stood a tall **Christmas tree** (81) hung all over with candles, trinkets and toys of every kind: **wooden horses** (82) , **dolls** (83) , and so on.
t16-14-3: The **perfumery** (84) , with its **tooth washes** and its various **perfumes**, gave off a very pleasant smell that rose to us.
t16-15-1: 15. — My grandfather was starting to get bored, so we went back down the great staircase. He stopped for a moment in front of an **astronomy chart** (85) showing, he told me, **comets** (a) , **eclipses of the moon and the sun** (b) , a compass rose with the **four cardinal points** (c) **(north, south, east and west)**, a map of the two **hemispheres** (d) , the **planets** (e) and the **solar system** (f) . I understood none of it, and I was far more interested in the braided livery of a **delivery boy** (86) who went by, and in the pretty **fans** (87) beside me, next to the **purses** (88) and the **wallets** (89) .
t16-16-1: 16. — I also admired on the counter some **feathers** (90) and **belt buckles** (91) , and the pretty **artificial flowers** (94) gracefully arranged in baskets. The **violets**, **wallflowers**, **hyacinths** (95) , **geraniums** (96) , **lilies** (97) and **nasturtiums** (98) were very well imitated.
t16-17-1: 17. — I asked my grandfather to buy me one of the **toothbrushes** (92) in a box beside the **hairpins** (93) . He agreed, and I went myself to pay for my purchase at the cash desk, beside which a large **parcel** (100) was being made up for a **customer** (99) .
t16-18-1: 18. — Suddenly there was a slight commotion among the people standing near the artistic **bronzes** (101) . A **thief** (102) had just been caught in the act by a **store detective** (103) while trying to rob someone. A policeman was sent for to **arrest** him, and just as we were leaving, the culprit was being led off to the police station.
